attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Millbank Charity Run 10K, Sunday 28 November 2027

From Daniel Mwangi, Event Coordinator, Millbank Community Association

The race is a 10K with 299 runners and starts at 09:00. On-site ambulance cover is set out in the attached paperwork from Halden Medical Transport.

First aid
Several of our members have done the first aid course through work, and they're happy to help out. We keep a good first aid box at the HQ tent, and another one goes in the lead car. In all our years we've only ever had blisters and scraped knees.

Heat, cold and water
We always tell runners to dress sensibly for the weather and to keep drinking, and it's all in the email we send them the week before. We'll be watching the forecast, and people here are used to all sorts of weather.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at Valley Regional Hospital, 14 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the top of Abbey Road with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
We'll all have our phones, and I'll send a list of numbers round the team the week before. The signal is usually fine around there.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Rhys Morgan, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Millbank Charity Run 10K | Sunday 28 November 2027
Organiser: Millbank Community Association
Race director: Daniel Mwangi
Reference: PH-34658

Overview
The Millbank Charity Run 10K is a 10K race of 10 km for 299 entrants, based in the Lakeshore area of Port Halden. The start is at 09:00 and the course closes at 11:00.

Course
The course runs in order along Abbey Road, Bell Street, Albion Road and Vine Street, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Victoria Road, Cross Avenue, Tram Street, Canal Road and Prince Street. The finish is in Clocktower Square.

Course dimensions
The course uses wide carriageways throughout. Abbey Road offers 16 m kerb to kerb, Albion Road about 9 m and Vine Street about 9 m, with footways of a further 3 m on each side. The field assembles on Abbey Road, and the finish is in Clocktower Square, an open paved area of around one and a half hectares.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Abbey Road from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Millbank website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Traffic arrangements for the Millbank Charity Run 10K, Sunday 28 November 2027

From Daniel Mwangi, Event Coordinator, Millbank Community Association

We have tried to think through what happens on the roads on race day. The race is a 10K, it starts at 09:00, and it goes through the Lakeshore area. The police traffic unit has told us by phone that it will attend.

Closing the roads
We need the following closures, and Signal Hill Traffic Services will put out the barriers and signs for us. Abbey Road from Linden Avenue to Ash Avenue, 07:30 until 11:30. Bell Street from Hatter Street to Ash Avenue, 07:30 until 11:30. Albion Road from Ash Avenue to Hatter Street, 07:30 until 11:30. Vine Street from Linden Avenue to Hatter Street, 07:30 until 11:30.

Crossings
Where we cross a major road we will have people stationed from 07:30 until the last runner is through. At Victoria Road, where it meets Albion Road, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Cross Avenue, where it meets Bell Street, there will be 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Tram Street, where it meets Bell Street, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Canal Road, where it meets Abbey Road, there will be 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor. At Prince Street, where it meets Abbey Road, there will be 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards and a supervisor.

Getting around the closures
We've worked out the way round for drivers and Signal Hill Traffic Services will sign it. Traffic off Abbey Road goes via Dock Road and Ferry Road, signed from Ash Avenue. Traffic off Bell Street goes via Station Road and Queen's Road, signed from Bridge Row. Traffic off Albion Road goes via Station Road and High Street, signed from Hatter Street. Traffic off Vine Street goes via Station Road and Church Road, signed from Hatter Street.

Emergency vehicles
We keep one lane clear the whole way, 3.5 metres or more, for ambulances and fire engines. Every barrier has someone with a radio on our channel, and they can have it open within two minutes. Our controller on the day has direct numbers for police and ambulance control.

Letting people know
We put the race on our Facebook page and in the club newsletter, and the local paper usually gives us a mention.

Afterwards
Once it's all over the team will collect the cones and barriers, and everyone can get back to normal.
